source.title: Double Descent in High-dimensional Linear Discriminant Analysis
source.authors: Yong-He Lu; Han-Lin Shang; Yan-Rong Yang; Ke-Han Zhao

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests double-descent behavior using a different model class and analysis: pseudoinverse LDA, with misclassification error measured as the feature-to-sample ratio varies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own theoretical risk results and simulation and ARCENE error outcomes. It cites prior double-descent results, which are not recorded as findings of this study. Values available only from plots are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: The study derives and simulates the test-error curve of pseudoinverse LDA as p/n varies across the interpolation point p≈n. That is a result on V4 (double descent beyond deep networks) in a new model class, with one sample-size observation bearing on V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that LDA risk can be non-monotone in p/n, showing double descent even in this classical linear method. Theorems give limits for general covariance when γ<1 and for isotropic covariance when γ>1, joining continuously at 1/2 at γ=1. Simulations and ARCENE extend this beyond the theory. They add that the global minimum fell in the over-parameterized region in their simulations, but heavy over-parameterization is likely not ideal with noisy features.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes pseudoinverse LDA with random-matrix limits and simulations, rather than testing deep-network size, epoch, or sample-size sweeps in the original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported curve changes with covariance structure, population separation, feature distribution, label and feature noise, redundant-feature proportion, and ARCENE feature-selection ordering. With bounded signal in the isotropic over-parameterized theory, error eventually returns toward 1/2.
record.problems: Many simulation outcomes are available only as plots, without numerical values or reported uncertainty intervals. The formal over-parameterized theorem covers only isotropic covariance and bounded Mahalanobis distance; several simulations use growing signal. Some non-Gaussian and ARCENE settings violate LDA assumptions, as the authors note.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise relevant results were left out.

untested.parts: No deep networks; the size axis is LDA feature dimension.
Only a text statement at fixed p from three sample sizes (Figure 4). No sample-size sweep near the threshold and no numbers.
No effective-complexity measure is defined or used to predict peak location across axes. The redundant-feature 'effective p' remark is informal.
Noise is varied, but no result shows the peak is driven by noise. Multiple peaks and optimally tuned regularization removing the peak are not tested.
Risk is not replotted against an effective parameter count.

missing.what: ARCENE comparison of shrinkage and regularized LDA (SLDA, MLDA, DLDA) with PLDA across γ. It could show whether regularization removes the γ≈1 peak; no row records these curves.
Authors' summary that in all simulated settings the global minimum is in the over-parameterized region, while noisy features cause a quick ascent there.
Under-parameterized U-shaped theoretical curves when signal grows with p (identity c∈{0.1,0.5,3}; compound symmetry ρ∈{0.1,0.3,0.5}).
missing.locator: Section 3.1, Figure 2; Appendix B Figure B.1

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Most simulation results are figure-only and carry no uncertainty. The bounded-signal theory predicts eventual re-ascent, while the growing-signal simulations show a sustained decline; the authors attribute the difference to signal growth. The tranche was changed to T3 because LDA is a new model class. The V5 and V6 links were removed because neither is tested in the form the version states.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies LDA feature dimension, not the size of deep networks.
No epoch- or training-time sweep is reported.
The reported more-data effect is at fixed feature dimension through a shift in the interpolation threshold; no general sweep of sample size near the threshold is reported.
The tested model class is LDA; the study does not establish the curve across all model classes.
Redundant features are used to discuss an effective feature count, but the paper does not test one complexity measure across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study varies label and feature noise. It does not test triple or multiple descent, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes a peak.
The study does not replot risk against an appropriate effective number of parameters or test whether that turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shape.

rows.subject: Pseudoinverse LDA classifier (Theorem 1)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical risk characterization as γ varies in the under-parameterized regime.
rows.value: Limit: Φ(−√(1−γ)∆² / (2√(∆² + 4γ))); for fixed ∆, error increases monotonically with γ and approaches 1/2 as γ ↑ 1.
rows.uncertainty: Convergence in probability; no error bar stated.
rows.note: With signal held fixed, this under-parameterized theoretical curve rises toward the threshold rather than showing the full fall-rise-fall pattern.
rows.check: Under-parameterized theory at fixed ∆ gives a monotone rise to 1/2 at γ=1 and no first descent. Only the ascent to the threshold peak appears.

rows.subject: Pseudoinverse LDA classifier (Theorem 2)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical risk characterization as γ varies in the over-parameterized regime.
rows.value: Limit: Φ(−√(γ−1)∆² / (2√(γ∆² + 4γ))); it decreases after γ = 1, reaches a minimum at an intermediate γ > 1, then tends back to 1/2 as γ → ∞.
rows.uncertainty: Convergence in probability; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The result has a second descent after the threshold, but with bounded signal the error later rises again.
rows.check: A second descent follows γ=1, but with bounded ∆ the error reaches a minimum and returns toward 1/2 as γ→∞.

source_check.correct: The limit is Φ(−√(γ−1)∆² / (2γ√(∆²+4γ))). The stated descent, intermediate minimum, and eventual return toward 1/2 at bounded ∆ are correct.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2, Theorem 2; Appendix A, concluding calculation of its proof.
source_check.problem: The denominator is transcribed incorrectly: the paper has 2γ√(∆²+4γ), not 2√(γ∆²+4γ).

rows.subject: Pseudoinverse LDA classifier
rows.operation_detail: Measured error across γ after flipping a percentage of responses.
rows.value: figure only; response flipping raises overall error, while increasing γ reduces error.
rows.note: The result shows an effect of label noise on error but does not establish that label noise drives the interpolation-threshold peak.
rows.check: Label flipping raises overall error, and error falls with γ. The text does not compare peak height with and without noise, so it cannot show the peak is noise-driven.

rows.subject: Pseudoinverse LDA classifier
rows.operation_detail: Measured error across γ with Gaussian noise added to a fixed percentage of feature columns.

conditions.value: Gaussian feature noise at varying levels

rows.value: figure only; higher feature-noise levels produce a more prominent increase in error as γ increases, including a second rise.
rows.note: The paper reports a second rise under noisy features, not multiple separate peaks.
rows.check: Relinked from V6 to V4. Feature noise makes error rise again at large γ, undoing the second descent. This is a later rise, not a noise-driven interpolation peak or multiple peaks.

rows.subject: Pseudoinverse LDA classifier
rows.operation_detail: Varied the percentage of irrelevant features and measured error as γ changes.
rows.value: figure only; the text says the error peak is postponed, and more redundant features give higher error at larger γ.
rows.note: The authors explain the postponed peak by saying the effective number of p is smaller; no quantitative effective-complexity measure is reported.
rows.check: Peak is postponed beyond p≈n and more irrelevant features raise error at large γ. V5 link removed: the 'effective p' remark is informal, defines no complexity measure, and covers only one axis.

rows.subject: Pseudo-LDA (PLDA)
rows.size_stated: p up to 1000; original data have 10,000 features and 100 samples
rows.operation_detail: Measured error while varying the number of randomly selected ARCENE features.
rows.value: figure only; the text reports a peak at error 0.5 when γ = 1 and decreasing error in the over-parameterized regime as features increase to 1000.
rows.uncertainty: The feature-selection experiment is averaged over 50 trials; the error-rate process is repeated 30 times.
rows.note: The paper reports substantial violations of normality and common-covariance assumptions in ARCENE.

rows.subject: Pseudo-LDA (PLDA)
rows.operation_detail: Measured PLDA error while varying γ using originally ordered ARCENE features.
rows.value: figure only; the text says PLDA has its highest error in the under-parameterized comparison and continuously decreasing error after a point at large γ.
rows.note: Table 1 reports PLDA minimum error 0.293 (γ = 0.7) under-parameterized and 0.202 (γ = 2.4) over-parameterized.
rows.check: Table 1: PLDA over-parameterized minimum 0.202 (γ=2.4) is below its under-parameterized minimum 0.293 (γ=0.7), and error keeps decreasing at large γ. A second descent with lower error is observed, not partial.
